sections.html:
Two layers of government share the job here. Every town, village and city in Calumet County contracts with its own assessor and has its own treasurer. The county treasurer's office in Chilton, at 206 Court Street, takes care of the county's part. Walk in Monday through Friday between 8 am and 4:30 pm, or call (920) 849-1457.

That office accepts every delinquent or postponed real estate payment for the county, collects the first installment for the City of New Holstein, settles the rolls with towns, villages, cities and school districts, sends out delinquent notices and processes parcels that become eligible for tax foreclosure.

A Real Property Lister sits in the same building. After a sale, the Transfer Form recorded at the Register of Deeds is forwarded to the treasurer's office, and that is how the owner and mailing details on the parcel get changed. The lister also assembles the tax rolls for the municipal assessors, whose values generally come in between late February and late May.

This is a small, largely rural county with Lake Winnebago on its western side, and Chilton is the seat. The 2020 count was 52,442 people, and the current estimate is 53,982. It falls within the Appleton metro area, and bits of Appleton, Kaukauna and Menasha extend into the northwest.

Farmland is taxed differently. Agricultural acreage is valued for what it can produce, which is why a farm parcel can carry a zero estimated market value on its bill. Sellers with acreage should read the bill carefully before a buyer asks about numbers.

You can pay everything by January 31 or split the bill, with the second half due July 31. Local treasurers mail real and personal property bills in early to mid December.

Splitting is open on any bill over $100. The first half goes to the local treasurer by January 31 and the second half to the Calumet County Treasurer by July 31. The first half must be paid in full and on time or the installment option is lost. Personal property tax is paid to the local treasurer in full by January 31 unless the bill shows an installment option.

WhenWhat happensWhere it goes
Early to mid DecemberReal and personal property tax bills are mailedLocal treasurer sends them
January 31Full payment, or the first installment on a bill over $100Local treasurer
February 1Interest and penalty of 1.5% per month begin on late paymentsCounty Treasurer collects delinquent real property tax
February and AugustDelinquent tax notices are mailedFrom the treasurer
July 31Second installmentCalumet County Treasurer, Chilton

Mailed payments need a postmark on or before the due date, and hand-delivered ones must reach the right treasurer that day. A payment that arrives within five business days after the due date can still count as timely under Wisconsin Statute 74.69, but treat that as a cushion and pay early.

A bill can include up to five main districts: the State of Wisconsin, Calumet County, a technical college, your municipality and a school district. Some parcels also fall in a special district for a lake, sewer or fire protection, and that district takes a share as well.

  • Towns: Brillion, Brothertown, Charlestown, Chilton, New Holstein, Rantoul, Stockbridge and Woodville.
  • Villages: Harrison, Hilbert, Potter, Sherwood and Stockbridge.
  • Cities: Brillion, Chilton and New Holstein, plus the Calumet County parts of Appleton, Kaukauna, Menasha and Kiel.
  • Technical colleges: Fox Valley, Moraine Park and Lakeshore.
  • School districts: Appleton, Brillion, Chilton, Hilbert, Kaukauna, Kiel, Kimberly, Menasha, New Holstein, Stockbridge and Wrightstown.

Two credits can lower the bill. The first dollar credit goes to any property with a structure on it, whatever its use or value. The lottery and gaming credit goes to property used as the owner's main home. The bill also shows the municipality's average assessment ratio, which compares assessed values with the state's estimate of fair market value taken from arm's length sales.

Because Calumet County assessors answer to individual towns, villages and cities, the Board of Review that hears your case sits in the municipality where your house is.

The timetable comes from Wisconsin Statute 70.47. A 45-day window opens on the fourth Monday of April, and the clerk posts a notice at least 15 days ahead (30 days when the municipality is revaluing). Move quickly:

  • Warn the clerk at least 48 hours before the first session, by writing or by phone, that you plan to object.
  • Turn in a written objection during the first two hours of that session. For good cause or extraordinary circumstances the board can excuse these steps.
  • Dispute the total of land plus improvements. Land alone or buildings alone cannot be challenged.
  • Put your own value in writing with supporting facts, and be prepared to testify under oath.

An assessor's value is presumed correct, and a tied vote leaves it standing. Beyond the board, an excessive assessment claim under Statute 74.37 is the next option. Ask your municipal clerk for this year's meeting date.

Late tax turns delinquent, the interest and penalty keep growing, and eventually the county may foreclose. Where you pay depends on the kind of tax: delinquent real property tax goes to the Calumet County Treasurer and delinquent personal property tax goes to your local treasurer.

Interest and penalty run 1.5% a month from February 1, with notices mailed in February and August. A parcel that reaches the foreclosure-eligible stage is processed by the treasurer. If you own one, phone the office to see where it stands and whether a county tax auction is coming.

Selling is easier before foreclosure than after it. Get a payoff figure early and settle the account at closing.

Ask the treasurer for the exact balance, then clear it through closing. What you owe depends on which installment has been paid, so last December's bill is only a starting point.

  • Call the Calumet County Treasurer at (920) 849-1457 and ask for the full amount owed on the parcel, interest and penalty included.
  • Confirm whether the first installment reached the local treasurer and whether the July 31 installment is still open.
  • Give the closing agent the parcel details so unpaid tax comes out of your sale proceeds.
  • Have the deed recorded at the Register of Deeds with the electronic transfer return. Under Statute 77.22(1) the grantor pays 30 cents per $100 of value or fraction, collected at recording.
  • After recording, the Real Property Lister changes the billing name and address on the parcel.

A house with a delinquent balance can still sell. The title work and the payoff only need to line up, which is easier when the tax figure is known early. A cash buyer skips the lender's review, though the tax payoff is still part of the closing.

faqs.q: When are Calumet County property taxes due?
faqs.a: January 31 for the full bill or the first installment, and July 31 for the second installment. The first goes to your local treasurer and the second to the Calumet County Treasurer in Chilton.

faqs.q: What interest does Calumet County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: The rate is 1.5% per month, counted from February 1. It applies to a late first or second installment once the unpaid tax is delinquent.

faqs.q: Who sets the value of my Calumet County home?
faqs.a: A municipal assessor does. Each town, village and city hires its own, and values go to the county's Real Property Lister, usually between late February and late May. The state separately estimates fair market value from arm's length sales for the bill.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Calumet County tax bill in two parts?
faqs.a: Yes, if the bill is over $100. Pay the first half to the local treasurer by January 31 to keep the option, and the second half to the county treasurer by July 31. A late first payment ends the installment option.

faqs.q: Which credits lower a Calumet County tax bill?
faqs.a: The first dollar credit and the lottery and gaming credit. The first goes to any property with a structure, and the second to property used as the owner's primary residence.
